units.title: Problem Set 1: one-dimensional kinematics
examples: car and bicycle: constant-velocity and accelerating motions, when and where they meet
elevator trip with acceleration, constant-speed and deceleration phases: position and velocity graphs
rocket accelerating upward then a stone released from it: height, time of flight
projectile thrown over a person to be caught at a distance: launch speed and angle
two cans thrown up at different times to meet at a given height

units.title: Problem Set 2: two-dimensional kinematics and Newton's laws
examples: stacked blocks with static friction: largest push for which they move together
bucket hanging from an accelerating truck: rope angle and tension

units.title: Problem Set 4: circular motion and Newton's laws
examples: block on an incline tied over a pulley to a hanging block: static friction range
velocity-dependent resistive force: integrate Newton's law for v(t) and distance
tension in a massive rotating rope with an end mass
rope over a fixed rod with friction (capstan): tension ratio, slipping mass
linear drag at low speed: terminal velocity and v(t)
two pulleys, two strings, two blocks: constraint and accelerations

units.title: Problem Set 5: momentum and impulse
examples: bullet embedded in a block: speed after, energy lost
acrobat grabs a clown in mid-air: speed after and maximum height
centre of mass of a uniform and a non-uniform rod
two particles attracting with an inverse-cube force: momentum and energy

units.title: Problem Set 6: momentum flow and centre of mass
examples: rowing across a river: relative velocity, landing point, time
astronauts playing catch: speeds after throwing and catching
two-stage rocket in empty space: final speed (rocket equation)
raindrop gaining mass as it falls: variable-mass equation

units.title: Problem Set 7: work and energy
examples: object sliding down an incline with friction: speed by the work–energy theorem
collision then sliding on a rough surface: distance from energy and momentum

units.title: Problem Set 10: rotational dynamics
examples: moments of inertia of a disc and a washer
compound pulley of two discs with hanging masses: angular acceleration
rod hinged to a wall held by a cable: tension and hinge force (static equilibrium)
person standing on a slope: normal forces on each foot

units.title: Problem Set 12: angular momentum
examples: rolling bicycle wheel: velocities of points on the rim
ball rolling without slipping inside a ring: angular speeds
cube sliding into a low ridge and tipping: minimum speed (angular momentum)
yo-yo rolling on an incline pulled by its string
billiard ball struck: rolling begins after sliding; final speed
